content:
Apple TV's current lineup is quite strong, featuring hit titles such as "Slow Horses," "Ted Lasso," "Dark Matter," and "Brothers," a new comedy starring Matthew McConaughey. But the hits keep coming—here's everything new coming to Apple TV in October.

"The Last First: Winter K2"

  • Date: October 2
  • Type: Movie
  • Category: Documentary

Directed by Amir Bar-Lev, "The Last First: Winter K2" tells a complex, gripping, and moving story that unpacks the extreme mountaineering industry and its ever-changing culture. The film focuses on a 2021 expedition in which Icelandic mountaineer John Snorri Sigurjónsson, together with the Pakistani father-and-son duo Ali Sadpara and Sajid Sadpara, set out to become the first people to summit K2 in winter—the most punishing season on the mountain. Along the way, they encounter YouTubing mountaineering influencers and their camera crews, clients from commercial guiding outfits, and a team of Sherpas led by the renowned Nims of Nepal. "The Last First: Winter K2" takes viewers to the frozen heights of K2, where unpredictable weather gives way to an unexpected, layered story—of strategy and determination, of class and caste, of wealth and power—all unfolding in the face of life and death.

"The Sisters Grimm" Season 2

  • Date: October 2
  • Type: Series
  • Category: Kids & Family

Two orphaned sisters navigate a town full of fairy-tale characters, facing both heroes and villains as they investigate the truth behind their parents' disappearance. Blending exploration, fantasy, and adventure, "The Sisters Grimm" delivers meaningful themes for viewers of all ages.

"Small Prophets"

  • Date: October 7
  • Type: Series
  • Category: Comedy

"Small Prophets" is a comedy about an eccentric character named Michael Sleep (played by Pearce Quigley). Since the disappearance of his beloved Clea seven years ago, Michael has been living an utterly ordinary life—working at a hardware store, visiting his father Brian (Sir Michael Palin)—all the while hoping Clea will return. One day, Brian shares an ancient recipe: rainwater, horse manure, and a touch of alchemy. Armed with the formula (if only half-believing in it), Michael sets out to create homunculi—tiny magical beings that can predict the future—hoping they can answer the biggest question on his mind: "Will I ever see Clea again?"

"Matchbox The Movie"

  • Date: October 9
  • Type: Movie
  • Category: Action

Based on Mattel's classic toy brand, "Matchbox The Movie" is a globetrotting, action-packed adventure about a group of childhood friends whose peaceful lives are upended when a CIA undercover agent named Sean (played by John Cena)—their long-lost former "big brother" figure—suddenly returns to their small town, accidentally dragging them into a world-saving international chase.

"Tenzing"

  • Date: October 16
  • Type: Movie
  • Category: Drama

Based on a true story, "Tenzing" tells the little-known tale of Tenzing Norgay (played by Genden Phuntsok), a gifted Himalayan mountaineer who, alongside New Zealand climber Edmund Hillary (played by Tom Hiddleston), became one of the first people to reach the summit of Mount Everest. Encouraged by his wife Dawa (played by Thinley Lhamo) and supported by expedition secretary Jill Henderson (played by Caitríona Balfe), Tenzing convinces Colonel John Hunter (played by Willem Dafoe) to let him join the British climbing expedition as a full member rather than just a porter. Where Western climbers saw "Everest" as a conquest, Tenzing honoured "Chomolungma" as a sacred mother goddess. What follows is an ascent full of tension—not only with the mountain itself, but between people of different backgrounds, classes, and ambitions. At the roof of the world, however, empire, class, and ambition fall away, leaving only two outsiders bound by mutual respect and trust. For Tenzing, the journey fulfils a lifelong dream and completes a spiritual calling.

"Where's Wanda?" Season 2

  • Date: October 21
  • Type: Series
  • Category: Dark Comedy

Apple's first German-language series, "Where's Wanda?" is a dark comedy about parents Dedo and Carlotta Klatt, who are desperate to find their missing 17-year-old daughter Wanda, who vanished without a trace months ago. With the police investigation going nowhere, the family decides to take matters into their own hands. With the help of their tech-savvy son Ole, they obtain surveillance equipment, pose as utility company workers, and wiretap nearly half the neighborhood—only to discover that behind closed doors, none of their neighbors are who they seem.

"Nocturne"

  • Date: October 30
  • Type: Series
  • Category: Crime Drama

The series follows Jonah Lynn (played by Liev Schreiber), a former soldier turned homicide detective. Tired of dodging bullets on the streets of Philadelphia, he moves to a small town in western Pennsylvania for a quieter life. But when the town—and his family—come under threat from a cunning serial killer named Jurek Walter (played by Graham), Jonah must protect everything he holds dear. With the search for Jurek's last missing victim reaching a critical stage, Jonah is forced to send his protégé, FBI agent Saga Bauer (played by Beetz), into the line of fire against Jurek himself. Just how far will Jonah go?

New episodes: "Slow Horses," "Brothers," and more

Apple TV will also roll out new episodes in October across a number of its currently airing series, including:

  • "Ted Lasso": The comedy starring Jason Sudeikis, airing through October 7
  • "Last Seen": A crime-thriller series, airing through October 7
  • "Slow Horses": The acclaimed British spy drama, airing through October 21
  • "Dark Matter": The sci-fi series starring Joel Edgerton, airing through October 30
  • "Brothers": The comedy starring Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson, airing through November 4

Which Apple TV October release are you planning to watch? Let us know in the comments.

Apple TV's monthly subscription is US$14.99, and you can also subscribe at a discount through the Apple One bundle.
